summary: git log shows the history of the repository: who made each commit, when, and why. Options narrow the list or show the changes inside each commit.
notes: Each commit has a hash, an ID of 40 letters and digits. The first 7 characters are enough to name a commit.
HEAD -> main in the log marks the commit you are on and the branch you are on.
git log -- scores.csv answers the question "when did this file change?"
pitfall: A long git log can fill the screen. Use --oneline or a number like -5 to keep it short.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with four commits on main.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add Zoe's score"
